analysis:
This PR moves the release toolchain pin from SDK 27.0 / Swift 6.4 to SDK 27.2 / Swift 6.4.2. The changed files are docs/operations/provider-release.md:611, mise.toml:12, scripts/provider_release_resume/identity.py:82 and scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh.

In prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh, DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN selects one of two modes (head 22-35). Mode `release` accepts only SDK 27.2 with Swift 6.4.2. Mode `qualification`, the DEFAULT, also accepts SDK 27.0 and any Swift 6.4.x. The script now scans DARKBLOOM_XCODE_APPLICATIONS (default /Applications) for Xcode*.app, newest first (head 97-119). It exports DEVELOPER_DIR to GITHUB_ENV when its choice differs from the image's Xcode (head 154-156), and that setting carries into the later Metal and signing steps. It also records the actual PROVIDER_SDK_VERSION (head 159) and points the wrapper symlink at script_dir instead of GITHUB_WORKSPACE (head 152). Every candidate and override comes from the CI runner image or the CI environment, which the workflow controls. No adversary in the threat model (ADV-001/002/003) controls these inputs, so no new attack surface was found.

The signing, notarization and hash identity (A-011, A-017, T-013, T-054) are computed from the final signed bytes and are unchanged. Toolchain selection does not affect the provenance or registration checks in identity.py.

identity.py:82 now hardcodes build_sdk_version 27.2 for resumed signing. A retained run built before this change (SDK 27.0) would be labelled 27.2. A downstream SDK-match check would likely fail closed, which is a correctness and availability concern, not a trust bypass.

Open items for integration (workflow files are not in this batch):
(1) Confirm the release-provider workflow build, qualify-sdk and signing jobs set DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN=release. Otherwise release builds silently accept SDK 27.0 or a non-6.4.2 Swift, contradicting doc line 611 ("final recorded SDK must match").
(2) Confirm the downstream consumer of build_sdk_version / PROVIDER_SDK_VERSION compares the two values and fails closed.
(3) The test file scripts/test-provider-release-toolchain.py was shown only as metadata and a partial patch.

No security regression is established from the supplied evidence.
